title: Meridian Quarterly, issue 12: a 32-page saddle-stitched print magazine, from empty document to press-ready PDF/X-4
domain: Page layout and prepress (spec 14.6, with colour 14.8 and the shell in 14.30)
deliverable: 32pp self-cover magazine, 210 x 280 mm trim, 3 mm bleed: two parent-page families, a threaded 8-page feature and departments, placed CMYK images, spec tables, footnotes, generated contents and index, a clean preflight, PDF/X-4 with marks and an output intent, an imposition plan and a collect-for-output package.

evidence_pin.method: Every E evidence was resolved to a line by the generator and every negative was a zero-hit git grep at the pin. No code was built or run.

panels_needed_together.source: STU-SHL-087 line 32226 is the default arrangement; the episodic row is this project's own need

reachable_without_hunting: Preflight status light in the status bar, always visible, one click to the preflight panel
Overset port marker on the frame, and an overset count that does not depend on the frame being on screen
Parent / page edit context: which one is being edited must always be visible
Text Frame tool, Picture Frame tool, Selection and Type within the first Tool Rail slots
Text Styles beside Character and Paragraph, without opening a dialog to apply a style
Swatches reachable from text and from frames, with the fill or stroke target plainly marked
Export recipe and last-used PDF preset reachable from FILE and from the preflight panel
workspace_switches: No switch is needed for layout, text and prepress: one Layout preset must carry the whole issue, per STU-SHL-055 presets gate nothing
Optional switch to the Type preset for a long copy-fit session
A raster fix should open the placed image in another tab and return on save with the link updated; not available today
what_would_feel_incoherent: WORST: the Layout Editor is one floating panel holding a private copy of the document. Its edits are not in the document the rest of the shell sees, are not saved, and its page view composes with a placeholder 0.5 em advance, so line breaks and overset on screen are not those of the PDF route, which shapes through hsk-studio-type.
Layers, Swatches, Appearance, Transform and Align act on the Run or vector document, and the layout panels act on the private copy, so one window has two sources of truth for the same layer.

Harness panels are a single floating window per surface; spec 14.30 requires docked groups of named panels. The layout editor's Pages, Threads, Styles, Tables, Find and Preflight sections must become the spec's separate panel identities in the Vulkan shell, not one long window.
Separations, overprint and ink limits exist for vector artboards but not for pages, so a print job has its prepress tools only in the wrong profile.

Soft proof tints the canvas composite while the page view is drawn elsewhere, so proofing cannot be judged on the layout surface. UNVERIFIED whether a page-spread document composites to that canvas at all.
Text colour is RGB on the style record in a CMYK job; a press designer will read that as the application not being for print.
Graphic frames are absent from the page view, so a magazine spread on screen shows text and no pictures.
checks_for_a_screenshot_reviewer: At 1920 x 1080 with the three docks open, a full spread at fit zoom is at least 60 percent of window width
No field-dense panel shares a tab group with a list-dense panel (STU-SHL-074)
Below 260 px docks turn to stacked compact form and do not clip (STU-SHL-073)
Margin, column, bleed, slug and guide colours are five distinct values and legible on white
Disabled commands stay visible with a reason (STU-SHL-018, STU-SHL-019)

gaps.what: No host reaches layout PDF export. export_pdf_with, glyph lowering from hsk-studio-type, page labels and outlines exist and are tested in their crate, but the harness has no hsk-studio-interop-layout dependency and no export command. The same holds for IDML export.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: It is the deliverable. Nothing else in a print project counts until a real page reaches a real PDF, and most of the engine is already there.

gaps.what: No layout command surface. RUN_COMMANDS has no layout id, so LayoutEdit, preflight and find cannot be driven by the command path of SMB-HARNESS-DRIVE-1; they are reachable only from Rust.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Every later check depends on it: without it neither a model nor this scenario's runner can operate layout out of process.

gaps.what: Layout state is not persisted. LayoutEditor edits a private snapshot; stories, flow, parents, long-document and style records never reach the package, and there is no reopen.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Work cannot survive a session, which rules out any real project and any recovery proof.

gaps.what: Placed graphics in layout: no place command, no graphic frame in the editor or page view, no CMYK image path to PDF, no clipping path, 38-field link record or relink.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: A magazine without pictures is not a magazine; this blocks the visual review of every spread.

gaps.what: Character and paragraph attribute model: no per-range size, tracking, kerning, baseline shift or OpenType features; no indents, spacing, tabs, drop caps, rules or keep options; no nested styles.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Matches truth-check rank 1. Output would be typographically unacceptable even once the PDF route works, but it does not stop a first PDF.

gaps.what: Print colour on layout: type styles hold StudioRgba only; frames cannot bind swatches; no working-space or policy command; no assign or convert; the PDF writer's Colour has no separation or overprint, so spot ink cannot reach the file.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: The file could carry a valid PDF/X-4 identification and still be wrong on press; ranks after pictures and type only because those block earlier steps.

gaps.what: Long-document host: TOC, index, sections, running heads, footnotes, cross-references and text variables have engine and Folio records but no LayoutEdit member or panel.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: High step count and cheap for what it unlocks, since the engines exist; it needs G2 and G3 first or the results vanish.

gaps.what: Document setup: custom trim and presets, facing and binding, bleed and margin edits, slug, page grid, baseline grid and guides in the host, document-wide layers.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: These are the first steps of every job. Records partly exist, so bleed and size can be stubbed by hand while the export path is proved.

gaps.what: PDF output options for press: stock PDF/X presets refuse for lack of a captured output intent; X-1a and X-3 refuse; no printer marks; the 88-field preferences record is connected to no exporter.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: X-4 can be set through ExportOptions directly, so a first file does not wait for it, but no printer will accept a job without marks when asked for them.

gaps.what: No independent PDF/X oracle. check_pdfx4 is the crate's own reading of ISO 15930-7 as recalled; the only veraPDF report on file is PDF/A-2b, and public veraPDF material found names PDF/A, PDF/UA and WTPDF but not PDF/X (UNVERIFIED against its full documentation).
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Small to decide, and it changes what may be claimed: the module comment names veraPDF as a possible X-4 validator, which this work could not confirm. It needs an Operator decision on the oracle, for example a commercial preflight run or a print provider check.

gaps.what: Autoflow, smart text reflow and primary text frames.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Manual threading works, so this is speed rather than possibility, though for long features the speed matters a great deal.

gaps.what: Text wrap and anchored objects: reflow accepts obstacles and anchors compute, but Folio stores no wrap record and no host reaches either.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Standard in features, and it depends on graphics (G5) existing first.

gaps.what: Preflight is 9 rules. No links, colour, ink, resolution, transparency, font, page-count or TOC-stale rules; profiles are neither stored, embedded nor exported; no preflight on export.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: A green light today means little for press: the failures a printer cares about are not checked. New rules need graphics and colour to exist first.

gaps.what: Editor composition is a placeholder: fixed 0.5 em advance. Also no move or resize of a frame and no parent edit canvas, in a shell being rebuilt on Vulkan.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: This decides whether the GUI can be trusted, but it is tied to the Vulkan rebuild, so it does not lead the list for the engine path.

gaps.what: Package and handoff: no collect-for-output, no fonts or links report, no print path; booklet is a plan with no output.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: End-of-job work; it is needed only when the rest can reach it.

gaps.what: Tables beyond structure: no table or cell styles, strokes or fills from a host, no CSV to table.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Structure works, so tables can be drafted; only formatting and data import are blocked.

gaps.what: Proofing: no spelling, no user dictionary, en-US hyphenation only, no language records in the host; find/change lacks formatting criteria; missing-font replace absent.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Matters for editorial quality, while this synthetic project can be proved without it.

gaps.what: Object styles and object effects on frames: object style engine has no host; four-target effects model is absent.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Consistency tool and finish; manual formatting is a workaround once frame properties exist.

gaps.what: Separations, ink coverage, overprint preview and flattener for layout pages: press has the Separator and coverage, but only the vector artboard route feeds them.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Prepress verification on top of the colour work in G8, so it comes after it.

gaps.what: Navigation in the PDF: outlines exist in the engine, but press has no link annotations, tags or alternative-text output.
gaps.why_it_ranks_here: Not required for press PDF/X; it matters for the digital edition, so it ranks last for this deliverable.

coverage.reading: The callable share overstates readiness. Callable steps are mostly in-memory LayoutEditor edits that cannot be saved, and no host can write a layout PDF, so the deliverable cannot be produced today from any entry point except a hand-written Rust program calling engine crates directly. No frame, thread, story, style, table or parent edit has a RUN_COMMANDS id; the corpus-reachable steps are a layer opacity, a PDF import and a checkpoint.
coverage.status_rule: callable: a RUN_COMMANDS or CLI command, or a public host API (LayoutEditor, Viewer) read at the pin. engine_only: a public engine function or record exists but a git grep of hsk-studio-harness, harness-core and harness-view finds no caller. missing: not found; evidence says where. Tests were not run, so nothing here proves that a call succeeds.

runner_notes.today: A runner cannot use command_id for most steps. api: entries are Rust calls: link hsk_studio_harness with feature layout-ui (hsk_studio_harness::layout_ui is public), hold one LayoutEditor, and call apply. engine_only steps need a hand-written Rust program over the engine crates. The JSONL loop of SMB-HARNESS-DRIVE-1 covers RUN_COMMANDS and timeline ids only, so it reaches this scenario's document.* and layer.* steps and nothing else, until G2 lands.
runner_notes.ordering: Steps are sequential. Do not skip a failed step silently: mark it blocked, keep going where state allows, and report status against this file, because the missing list is the purpose.
runner_notes.fixtures: Generate all inputs from a fixed seed into a temp dir. Reuse the repo font and ICC fixtures named in input_assets. No proprietary profile, font or image. The synthetic CMYK profile proves mechanics only, not press colour.
runner_notes.determinism: PDF export is deterministic when PdfX4 created and modified dates come from the runner (no clock is read, crates/hsk-studio-press-write/src/export.rs). Fix the dates, the seed, the fonts and the composition version. UNVERIFIED: the determinism of a whole magazine, since tests cover smaller documents.
